summary: For the 'Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer' challenge, we developed an interactive Martian outpost simulation game focused on Arcadia Planitia, designed to make space-themed STEM education engaging and accessible. The project addresses the oversimplification of engineering trade-offs in aerospace learning by incorporating real environmental and geological metrics of Arcadia—such as subsurface water ice accessibility, weather, and radiation data—into a gamified experience. Players must balance resource management, power generation, and life support constraints within this prime prospective landing site. This project is important because it transforms complex aerospace engineering and planetary colonization principles into an intuitive, interactive tool, inspiring the next generation of space explorers and learners.
details:
Project Overview & Functionality:

For the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer), we developed an interactive Martian outpost simulation game centered on Arcadia Planitia. The project allows users to experience the critical engineering trade-offs and decision-making required to sustain a human base on Mars, balancing life support, power generation, and vital resources based on real planetary parameters.

Technologies & Development Stack:

- Frontend & Logic: Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

- 3D Graphics & Rendering: Developed immersive 3D graphics and visual environments using Three.js powered by WebGL.

- Development Tools: Developed locally using Live Server for real-time testing and rapid iteration.

- AI Assistance: Leveraged ChatGPT to assist with coding logic, structure optimization, and troubleshooting.

- Deployment: Hosted and deployed live via Netlify Drop (https://toinfinityandbeyondd.netlify.app/) to ensure instant, public accessibility for judges and users.

Creativity & Impact:

Our team focused on transforming oversimplified aerospace engineering concepts into an immersive, educational web experience. By tackling the specific environmental and logistical challenges of Arcadia Planitia, the project bridges the gap between complex space exploration principles and interactive STEM learning.
